<<chapter=I>>
<<my_title=Arrival by Water>>
<<chsum=Ada Quill reaches Low Harbor and learns that her employer is gone.>>
<<top_bar>>
The ferry at |places|Low Harbor|| – A debt of |numbers=9|nine|| crowns – The
cartographer hires a boy – Salt on the wind.
<<bottom_bar>>

The ferry came into |places|Low Harbor|| on the {h_p7_tide}last tide of
|time|October, 1871||{h_p7_tide/}, riding so low that the |animals|gulls|| walked its
rail like inspectors. Ada Quill stepped off with a {c_p7_brass}brass
{cl_p7_theo}theodolite{cl_p7_theo/} in one hand{c_p7_brass/} and a letter of credit in the
other, and neither was worth what she had been promised.

The harbormaster was a narrow man named Osric Penn who
{l_p7_tin}kept his ledgers in a {m_p7_biscuit}biscuit tin{l_p7_tin/}. He told her{m_p7_biscuit/} the
survey office had closed in the spring and that the |numbers=9|nine||
crowns owed to her were owed, in turn, by a man who had
drowned. She thanked him. It was, she said, the most
complete account of a debt she had ever received.
